verses.text: These are more proverbs of Solomon, copied down by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
God's glory is to keep a matter hidden. The glory of kings is to search it out.
The sky is high, the earth is deep, and nobody can fully search out a king's heart.
Remove the impurities from silver, and the refiner has something to work with.
Remove wicked people from the king's presence, and his throne will stand firm on righteousness.
Don't hype yourself up in front of the king or claim a place among important people.
It's better to hear, “Come up here,” than to be moved down in front of the ruler you're standing there looking at.
Don't rush to take someone to court. What will you do when your neighbor proves you wrong and shames you?
Talk the case through with your neighbor, and keep other people's secrets,
or someone may hear what you did and shame you, and the bad reputation will stick.
The right word at the right time is like golden apples set in silver.
Wise correction to someone ready to listen is like a gold earring or a piece of pure gold jewelry.
A reliable messenger is like the chill of snow in harvest season. They refresh the people who sent them.
Someone who brags about a gift they never give is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
Patience can persuade a ruler. Gentle words can break a bone.
Found some honey? Eat just enough. Too much and you'll throw it up.
Don't show up at your neighbor's place too often, or they'll get tired of you and start to hate you.
A false witness against a neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Trusting someone unreliable in a crisis is like chewing on a bad tooth or standing on an injured foot.
Singing to someone with a heavy heart is like taking their coat in cold weather or pouring vinegar on soda.
If your enemy is hungry, give them food. If they're thirsty, give them water.
You'll pile burning coals on their head, and the LORD will reward you.
The north wind brings rain. Talking behind someone's back brings angry faces.
It's better to live in a corner of the roof than share a house with a wife who's always picking fights.
Good news from far away is like cold water when you're thirsty.
Someone who does right and gives in to the wicked is like a muddy spring or a polluted well.
Too much honey isn't good for you. Chasing your own honor isn't honorable.
A person with no self-control is like a ruined city with its walls down.
